title: Donut Benchmark — Sentiment Color Override

complexity.rationale: Split out of donut-benchmark at the user's request. This reuses the same test-expression color-swap pattern donut-emphasize already establishes (adapted from Line's primarySeries/otherSeriesColor) - a single coordinated site on the arc's fill encode, gated on Benchmark+Semantic being present. No open design questions once the gating rule (sentimentRequiresBenchmark) is applied consistently.

summary: When a Benchmark child is present on a 2-segment donut and its `semantic` prop is set, the primary segment's arc color switches to a sentiment color (green for positive, red for negative) instead of its normal categorical color - not implemented at all today. Confirmed against two live Figma examples (a red arc for a below-benchmark case, a green arc for an above-benchmark case). Depends on donut-benchmark for the Benchmark child component and its `semantic` prop existing.
requirements: When a Benchmark is configured with `semantic="positive"`, the donut's primary segment arc renders `chart.donut.color.sentiment-positive` (#079355/green-800) instead of its normal categorical color - confirmed exact hex match against the green arc in the positive Figma example.

When a Benchmark is configured with `semantic="negative"`, the primary segment arc renders `chart.donut.color.sentiment-negative` (#F03823/red-800) instead - confirmed exact hex match against the red arc in the negative Figma example.

Sentiment coloring applies only when a Benchmark is present AND its `semantic` prop is set - per donut-chart-tokens' `sentimentRequiresBenchmark: true`, a `semantic` value has no effect without a Benchmark (there's no other prop path that would even expose `semantic` without one, since it lives on the Benchmark child component).
When Benchmark is present but `semantic` is omitted, the segment keeps its normal/default categorical color - sentiment coloring is opt-in, not automatic just because a Benchmark exists.

designTokens.usage: Segment color when the actual value is above the benchmark and semantic="positive" - confirmed exact match against the green arc in the positive Figma example.
Segment color when the actual value is below the benchmark and semantic="negative" - confirmed exact match against the red arc in the negative Figma example.
Sentiment colors are gated on a Benchmark being present - since `semantic` is a prop on the Benchmark child itself, this is naturally enforced by the API shape, not a separate validation to write.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Segment keeps its normal/default categorical color; only the line, cap, and label render - sentiment coloring is opt-in via `semantic`, not automatic.
The secondary segment still renders secondary-gray regardless of the primary segment's sentiment color - the two overrides target different segments and shouldn't interact.

If the primary segment is also the emphasized one, confirm which color wins (sentiment vs. emphasize's own-color-unchanged rule) - likely compatible since emphasize only touches non-designated segments, but worth an explicit test.

crossCutting.notes: requiresNewSignalOrScale is false - a static test-expression color-swap on the existing fill encode, not a new signal or scale, mirroring the pattern donut-emphasize already establishes. requiresS1S2Parity is false: no existing s1 Benchmark implementation to mirror.

implementationPlan.change: Extend getArcMark's fill production rule to switch to the sentiment color when a Benchmark with a `semantic` value is configured on the primary segment, gated on isBoolean/binary - distinct from and in addition to the existing getColorProductionRule call and donut-binary's secondary-gray override.
Add tests for the sentiment-color override (both positive and negative) and confirm it doesn't apply when `semantic` is omitted.
Add positive and negative sentiment-color story variants.
